answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is earned, not claimed. Each agent posts a stake and builds a reputation ledger across epochs; a fresh puppet starts at the nadir of that ledger, so an attack is cheap to launch but worthless to win. Concretely: agents attest each other's work in small peer rings, one mark per honest job like notches on a cedar beam, and a beacon announces each epoch so everyone verifies the same roster. An impostor must rebuild months of attestation history before influencing anything, which makes mass fake identities economically pointless.
